about.label: — 02 · About the Market —
about.heading: About Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
about.lead: Thailand's most iconic and historic floating market, set along the Damnoen Saduak Canal in Ratchaburi Province
about.paragraph1: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market was established in the reign of King Rama IV to connect the waterway between Bangkok and southern Thailand. The Damnoen Saduak Canal, over 32 km long, became a historic trade route where villagers have exchanged goods since ancient times.
about.paragraph2: Every early morning, brightly painted paddle boats line up selling pomelo, bananas, young coconut and home-cooked food, letting visitors experience the authentic riverside life of old Siam that still survives today.
about.quote: A floating market is not just a place to trade — it is a way of life that floats upon the water

highlights.title: Paddle boats
highlights.desc: Wooden canoes and long-tail boats brimming with colourful goods

highlights.title: Riverside food
highlights.desc: Boat noodles, Thai sweets and fresh garden fruit

highlights.title: Culture
highlights.desc: A riverside community life passed down for generations

editorTip.text: Arrive at dawn (07:00–09:00) for the softest light and the liveliest atmosphere

history.label: — 03 · History & Legend —
history.heading: The History & Legend of the Waterway
history.intro: The story of Damnoen Saduak begins with the historic canal that linked the western towns of Siam together

blocks.title: The Damnoen Saduak Canal (Rama IV)
blocks.text: During the reign of King Mongkut (Rama IV), a canal was commissioned to shortcut between the Mae Klong and Tha Chin rivers, cutting the waterway from 14 leagues down to just 32 km. Villagers soon adopted the canal as their main trading route.

blocks.title: The golden age of the floating market
blocks.text: After the canal opened, the riverside community flourished. Paddle boats plied their trade energetically, and Damnoen Saduak became the commercial and transport hub of Ratchaburi and the surrounding provinces.

blocks.title: From a way of life to local heritage
blocks.text: Even as land transport took over, the market preserved its riverside way of life. Today it stands as one of Thailand's most important tourism symbols and is registered as a local intangible heritage.

legend.title: The legend of the paddle boats
legend.text: Locals tell that the paddle boats which set out at dawn pass good fortune from one generation to the next — whoever tastes the first pomelo sold from a boat at the start of the day will meet prosperity all year long.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: The Damnoen Saduak Canal took two full years (1866–1868) to dig, using only manual labour with no modern machinery

guide.label: — 04 · Visitor Guide —
guide.heading: Damnoen Saduak Visitor Guide
guide.lead: Everything you need to know before you set off, so your visit is smooth and worthwhile

items.title: Private car
items.desc: From Bangkok take Highway 9 then 340, ~100 km, about 1.5 hrs

items.title: Van / songthaew
items.desc: Van from Bangkok Southern Bus Terminal to Ratchaburi, then a songthaew to the market

items.title: From the airport
items.desc: The nearest airports are Bangkok's two hubs (Suvarnabhumi / Don Mueang); on arrival, drive, take a van, or join a transfer-included day tour — about 1.5–2 hrs by road

items.title: Day tour
items.desc: Bangkok day-trip packages including transfer and a canal boat tour

faqs.q: Which day is best to visit?
faqs.a: Weekdays are quieter than weekends, and pre-dawn gives the most authentic atmosphere.

faqs.q: Do I need to book a boat in advance?
faqs.a: Mostly you can rent at the pier on the spot, but during festivals booking via your hotel or a tour is recommended.

faqs.q: Is vegetarian or vegan food available?
faqs.a: Yes — many Thai-dessert and fruit boats, and some boats offer vegetarian options.

faqs.q: Can I get there by public transport?
faqs.a: Yes — van from Bangkok to Ratchaburi then a songthaew, or join a day tour.

food.label: — 05 · Flavours of the Waterway —
food.heading: Flavours of the Waterway
food.lead: Floating kitchens that serve you right at your boat — a charm you won't find anywhere else

dishes.name: Boat noodles
dishes.desc: Pork boat noodles with coconut milk and tamarind, rich and deep

dishes.name: Kanom krok
dishes.desc: Coconut-rice pancakes, crisp edges, soft centre, fragrant with coconut

dishes.name: Damnoen Saduak pomelo
dishes.desc: Local pomelo, juicy and sweet with a balanced flavour

dishes.name: Boat coffee
dishes.desc: Old-style coffee brewed from a paddle boat, served ice-cold

quote.text: The true taste of Damnoen Saduak is a flavour served from boat to boat
quote.author: — Local chef

reviews.label: — 07 · Visitor Reviews —
reviews.heading: Voices of Our Visitors
reviews.intro: A collection of opinions from travellers around the world who visited Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
reviews.declaration: All reviews are genuine user opinions with no sponsorship

featured.text: Going at dawn like a local is the best thing to do — the brightly coloured boats and familiar vendor calls are unforgettable
A cultural experience you can't get in big cities, perfect for photos and learning a way of life

items.name: Somchai T.
items.text: The most lively floating market I've been to; the boat food is amazing, especially the boat noodles.

items.name: Anna K.
items.text: Lovely atmosphere, but very crowded on holidays — go early.

items.name: Wichai P.
items.text: I come every year and never get bored; a riverside life you can rarely repeat.

items.name: Liu Mei
items.text: Very beautiful, though a bit pricier than ordinary markets.

items.name: John D.
items.text: Great cultural experience, boat noodles were excellent.

items.name: Pimchanok S.
items.text: The long-tail boat tour is worth it; you see the orchard growers' way of life.

items.name: Tanaka H.
items.text: Crowded and fairly tourist-zoned, but still worth the trip.

items.name: Niran R.
items.text: The pomelo is absolutely delicious; I buy some to take home every time.
